code_first.q: Trace a function calculating uncompressed image pixel data using two parameters.
code_first.code:
function imageBits(pixels,depth)
    return pixels * depth
endfunction
print(imageBits(50,8))
p: Predict the returned number of bits.
Change depth from 8 to 16 in the call.
Explain what colour depth means and why a function returns the result.
code_first.a: imageBits(50,8) returns 400 bits. Passing 16 bits per pixel returns 800 bits. Colour depth is the number of bits used to encode each image pixel; returning a result allows the caller to reuse it (e.g. convert bits to bytes). This excludes metadata and compression.

original_exam_questions: Explain one difference between a function and a procedure. [2 marks]
A function returns a value; a procedure performs statements without necessarily returning a value.
State the role of parameters. [2 marks]
They pass input values into a subprogram.
Give one benefit of modular programming. [2 marks]
Reduces duplication, simplifies testing or maintenance.

optional_original_challenge.coreHint: pixels × depth gives bits. The return value is used by the print call.

stretch.task: Call imageBits with two different colour depths, then convert each result into bytes.
stretch.hint: Call imageBits(50,8) and imageBits(50,16); divide each returned bit count by 8.
stretch.answer: 50 pixels at 8 bits/pixel → 400 bits = 50 bytes. At 16 bits/pixel → 800 bits = 100 bytes, excluding metadata.

mastery.task: Write a function countAbove(values,limit) that returns how many array items exceed a passed limit. Test equality and an empty list.
mastery.hint: Parameter limit changes the comparison; count starts at zero.
mastery.answer: For [2,5,8] with limit5, answer1 (only8); with limit1, answer3; empty list returns0. Iterate the array, increment only when item>limit, and return count.
